title: History 14: The speed era: LCM, turbo and distillation

questions.q: What is the primary architectural shift described in the 'speed era' of diffusion models?
options: Moving from CPU to GPU processing
Shifting from iterative refinement to direct prediction
Replacing UNet backbones with Transformer architectures
Increasing the resolution of the latent space
questions.answer: Shifting from iterative refinement to direct prediction
questions.why: The lesson states that the speed era covers the 'architectural shift from iterative refinement to direct prediction' and that the question changes from 'how do we denoise accurately?' to 'how do we predict the final state directly?'

questions.q: In the context of Latent Consistency Models (LCMs), what does the function F_theta(z_t, t) learn to predict?
options: The derivative f(z_t, t) of the PF-ODE
The clean latent z_0 directly from the noisy latent z_t
The next noisy latent z_{t-1} in the sequence
The noise schedule sigma for the current step
questions.answer: The clean latent z_0 directly from the noisy latent z_t
questions.why: The text explains that LCMs learn a function that 'directly maps any point on the trajectory to the endpoint z_0' and that 'the LCM predicts the clean latent z_0 directly from the noisy latent z_t'.

questions.q: According to the lab results, what was the calculated speedup factor when comparing the standard 50-step process to the 4-step distilled process?
questions.why: The lab results section explicitly lists 'RESULT speedup_factor = 12.5' and explains that this proves the distilled model is 12.5 times faster in terms of step count.

questions.q: Why is a lower CFG scale (e.g., 1.0-2.0) typically recommended for LCMs compared to standard diffusion models?
options: To reduce the computational cost of the forward pass
Because the model has already learned the guidance during distillation
To prevent the model from overfitting to the training data
To ensure the noise schedule remains linear
questions.answer: Because the model has already learned the guidance during distillation
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section states that LCMs are sensitive to CFG scale and that a lower CFG is recommended 'because the model has already learned the guidance during distillation'.

questions.q: What is the specific training cost mentioned for a high-quality 768x768 LCM in the 'Go deeper' section?
questions.why: The 'Go deeper' section cites the paper by Luo et al., noting that 'a high-quality 768x768 LCM takes only 32 A100 GPU hours for training'.
